subject: Renewal uplift: OliveHealth midcycle capacity + co-term ask
messages:
From: Jordan Dawson <j.dawson@olivehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OliveHealth renewal + midcycle uplift — request for options

Hi Lauren,

We’re moving toward our annual renewal but usage has spiked ~40% across our inference pipelines. We expect this to be durable through Q4 and want to evaluate options for adding capacity midcycle and aligning the renewal date with our fiscal year (co-term). Procurement asked me to surface:

- Pricing on incremental capacity (monthly usage top-up vs annualized commit)
- Any incentive/discount for co-terming and committing to a higher annual run-rate
- Timeline for amendment and whether we can get a single PO that covers the uplift and the renewal amendment

Attaching our current MA and draft SOW for context (OliveHealth_MA_v3.xlsx, SOW_renewal_draft.pdf). We’re targetting signed amendment by 2026-06-15 to match procurement cycles.

Can you put together 1–2 straightforward options we can share with finance/procurement? Also happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Dawson
Head of ML Platforms, OliveHealth
procurement@olivehealth.com

--
Attachment: OliveHealth_MA_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: SOW_renewal_draft.pdf (pdf stub)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Dawson <j.dawson@olivehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OliveHealth renewal + midcycle uplift — request for options

Jordan — thanks for the context and the attachments. Looping in Aditya (sales lead), Ben (finance), and Marissa (AE) to align. Below are two clean pathways we can offer — short bullets so procurement can compare quickly. Happy to convert to a formal amendment once you pick a path.

Option A — Staged annualize (recommended)
- OliveHealth commits to annualize the uplift: convert the additional 40% into an annual reserved commitment for the remaining contract term.
- Concession: 15% discount on the incremental annualized units (applies only to uplift portion).
- Benefits: predictable unit pricing, lower unit cost than pay-as-you-go, keeps main contract intact.
- Conditional: must sign amendment and PO by 2026-06-15 for discount to apply.

Option B — Temporary top-up (low friction)
- Add a monthly top-up bucket to cover current spike; billed at standard usage rates (no discount) and pro-rated.
- Benefits: fastest to implement, no long-term commitment required.
- Drawback: higher unit cost compared to annualized commit.

Operational notes:
- Co-terming: we can align the renewal date to OliveHealth’s fiscal year in the same amendment; that triggers a single consolidated invoice path.
- Legal/PO: we can accept a single PO that references the signed amendment; legal will require the redline but this is routine.
- Timeline: Aditya / Marissa — if Olive picks Option A, we’ll prepare an amendment + redline doc today and expedite to legal.

Jordan — if you want, schedule a 30-minute call and we’ll walk procurement through tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: redline_amendment.docx (word doc stub)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OliveHealth renewal + midcycle uplift — request for options

Quick finance read:
- Option A (annualize) with 15% uplift discount on the incremental units is borderline acceptable to margin but unlocks retention and predictable spend — I can sign off if we add a 12-month minimum for the uplift and require the 2026-06-15 execution date.
- If they push for a longer-shaped discount (e.g., 20% or applied across base), we need exec approval.

Proposed tweak (to keep things simple):
- Approve 15% discount on the uplift if OliveAnnualizes the uplift for >= 12 months and signs amendment by 2026-06-15.
- If they prefer top-up (Option B) we accept but no discount; encourage conversion to annualize within 90 days to capture retrospective credit (one-time).

Marissa / Aditya — we should include a one-paragraph economics note in the amendment describing the scoring period and conversion mechanics so procurement can see the math. I’ll draft.

-ben
Ben Carter
VP Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Dawson <j.dawson@olivehealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@olivehealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OliveHealth renewal + midcycle uplift — request for options

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear options. Procurement is pushing for the 15% concession on the uplift, and they want the co-term alignment included so we can issue a single PO. Two follow-ups from them:

1) They request that the amendment explicitly states a 60-day invoice/payment window after PO receipt.
2) They would like the SOW updated to call out the uplift buckets by environment (dev/staging/prod) — they want usage split visibility for audit.

We can commit to Option A with the conditions: sign by 2026-06-15 and 12-month annualization on the uplift. If you can send the redline amendment and SOW updates by COB Thursday (2026-06-03) procurement will prepare the PO and routing.

Let me know if the 60-day net payment window is feasible or if you need alternate wording.

Jordan
Jordan Dawson
Head of ML Platforms, OliveHealth
